fr:title.text: Normal forms in Cubical Type Theory

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Normal forms in Cubical Type Theory

fr:mainmatter.html:p: This note documents the specification of normal forms in cubical type theory. The definition is already present in the proof of normalization for cubical type theory, but we present it in a more traditional style explicitly for reference.

We give a moderately motivated exposition of exponentiable locales and the construction of exponentials in \textsf {Loc}, without assuming prior knowledge of exponential topological spaces or continuous posets.

fr:title.text: Synthetic Tait Computability the Hard Way

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Synthetic Tait Computability the Hard Way

fr:mainmatter.html:p: We walk through a few proofs of canonicity and normalization, each one with more aspects dissected and re-expressed in category theory, so that readers can compare the difference across proofs. During this process we isolate the different ideas that make up the proofs. Finally we arrive at synthetic Tait computability as proposed by J. Sterling. We also give a synthetic proof for parametricity of system F.

The following is a list of open (to my knowledge) problems that I’m interested in, with some thoughts on them. They are mostly in type theory, constructive logic and computability theory. I think about them from time to time, and if any problem is already solved in the literature, or has a new claimed solution, please contact me!

fr:title.text: Strongly total functions on Church numerals

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Strongly total functions on Church numerals

fr:mainmatter.html:p: What are all the total functions f : \mathbb {N} \to \mathbb {N} on natural numbers such that there exists an untyped \lambda -calculus term t such that t c_n (where c_n is the n-th Church numeral) is strongly normalizing for each n, and evaluates to c_{f(n)}? This is raised on MathOverflow.

In some sense, this is asking for a kind of limit on type systems that guarantee strong normalization. This class of total functions includes for example all the functions of type \mathbb {N} \to \mathbb {N} in system \mathrm {F}, where \mathbb {N} is encoded as \forall \alpha . (\alpha \to \alpha ) \to (\alpha \to \alpha ). These are the functions provably total in second order Peano arithmetic. Similarly system \mathrm {F}\omega gives all the functions provably total in higher order logic. These are all we get out of the \lambda -cube.

However, note that it’s not necessarily true that system \mathrm {F} can only provide us with these functions. It is possible that a term t has the property that each t c_n is typable (hence strongly normalizing) in system \mathrm {F}, but the types assigned to t or c_n depends on n. I’m also interested to see if there are these wild total functions.

Perhaps one direction of attack is to consider higher order logic equipped with stronger and stronger large cardinal axioms. We then somehow translate them to strongly normalizing type systems (with more and more universes).

fr:title.text: Dimensionlity of the rational number locale

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Dimensionlity of the rational number locale

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Classify the locales \mathbb {Q}^n up to homeomorphism. This is raised on MathOverflow.

It is well-known that \mathbb {Q} is not homeomorphic to \mathbb {Q}^2 as locales, which is in stark contrast with topological spaces where \mathbb {Q}^n are all homeomorphic. The proof is a delicate analysis on rectangles on the rational plane. Perhaps similar arguments can be carried out on higher dimensional spaces, but I haven’t given too much thought to it.
Formalize, or prove the impossibility for a definition of (\infty , 1)-categories in the style of synthetic homotopy theory in HoTT.
Defining \infty -categories following the usual, classical definition in HoTT is generally considered unproblematic, and just a matter of effort. There has been various projects working towards this.

A definition of \infty -categories synthetically should have the correct interpretation in the canonical model of HoTT in \infty -groupoids (or more concretely, simplicial sets), up to equivalence. We should also be able to extract the \hom -types, and define composition and the n-associator for each concrete number n. More generally, the axioms developed by Cisinski and others should be provable.
There has been various approaches to defining \infty -categories in extensions of HoTT. They generally correspond to the two styles of defining categories:

html:ul.html:li: Defining \hom -sets as families of sets over the collection of objects. Generalizing to \infty -categories requires arbitrarily long chains of dependencies. This is the idea of the work of displayed type theory.

Defining the total collection of arrows, with two projections \operatorname {dom} and \operatorname {cod}. Generalizing to \infty -categories requires the definition of (semi-)simplicial spaces, which require an infinite tower of coherences between these projection maps. This leads to the work of two-level type theory.

fr:title.text: The theory of presentable and accessible categories in type theory

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The theory of presentable and accessible categories in type theory

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Is it possible to develop the theory of presentable and accessible categories in a constructive (or even predicative) type theory? Barring this, how can we develop this theory in a type-theory idiomatic way?
It is known that the classical theory of presentable and accessible categories heavily relies on the axiom of choice. There are several questions on MathOverflow on this topic:

html:li.fr:link: Locally presentable and accessible categories without the axiom of choice?
Accessibility of small categories without choice
Obstructions to the theory of locally presentable categories without choice

fr:mainmatter.html:p: We can avoid a lot of choice unique up to unique isomorphism in a univalent type theory. It may also be possible to redefine notions of size using an inductive-recursively defined Tarski universe. I suspect this to be easier to use than trying to develop a theory of cardinals.

fr:title.text: Recursively realizable one-variable formula in propositional logic

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Recursively realizable one-variable formula in propositional logic

fr:mainmatter.html:p: What are all the propositional formulas involving one propositional variable that are realizable with recursive functions? In other words, what propositions are true in the computable world?

Constructive logic is realizable with computable functions, and so we can restrict our attention to the free Heyting algebra generated by one element, also known as the Rieger–Nishimura lattice, and asking if any proposition other than \top is realizable. According to this survey, although there are propositions unprovable in constructive logic but realizable computably, the existence of such one-variable propositions is still open.

fr:title.text: The orthogonal and unitary groups in synthetic homotopy theory

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The orthogonal and unitary groups in synthetic homotopy theory

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Define the orthogonal groups \mathrm {O}(n) and the unitary groups \mathrm {U}(n) in synthetic homotopy theory, together with their actions on the spheres of corresponding dimensions. Their deloopings as well as the direct limits \mathrm {O}, \mathrm {BO} etc. are also of interest. These definitions are necessary for the study of Bott periodicity, as well as the J-homomorphism in the homotopy groups of spheres.

There has been work on defining the tangent unit sphere bundle of spheres. It is plausible that we can build on this construction to define the orthogonal group. It is however unclear how we would define the group operation. See also these slides.

Specify a schema of inductive definitions that can handle arbitrary interleaving, nesting and dependency of induction and recursion. Prove or disprove the consistency, canonicity and normalization of these inductive definitions, as well as their compatibility with excluded middle, the axiom of choice and univalence.

Agda is extremely permissive on the validity of inductive definitions, far surpassing any literature. The declaration and definitions can be arbitrarily interleaved, and later definitions can refer to previous declarations freely (subject to termination checking). The strict-positivity checking is an “open” condition, meaning that each new feature of the type theory adds to the possible inductive definitions. So a “closed” approach such as reducing inductive types to \mathsf {W}-types seems inappropriate.

Some of these inductive types have been found to be inconsistent, or incompatible with excluded middle or univalence. However, fixing these inconsistencies reactively is not an ideal solution. Given that a large portion of these definitions seems intuitive, it should be possible to establish at least their consistency relative to set theory with well-known large cardinal axioms. See also this StackExchange question.
Define an elementary \infty -topos version of the effective topos. In particular, the 1-truncated objects should recover exactly the effective topos.

There has been a line of work defining and working with the effective 2-topos. On the other hand, trying to directly define assemblies in cubical sets gives the cubical assemblies, which unfortunately does not satisfy some principles that we expect of the effective topos, such as the Church thesis. There are ways to fix this problem, but it is ad hoc and doesn’t seem to be satisfactory as an answer to the question.

The following is a list of open (to my knowledge) problems that I’m interested in, with some thoughts on them. They are mostly in type theory, constructive logic and computability theory. I think about them from time to time, and if any problem is already solved in the literature, or has a new claimed solution, please contact me!

fr:link.title: Spectral sequence of a tower of fibrations

html:li.fr:link: Spectral sequence of a tower of fibrations

fr:mainmatter.html:p: On a computer, you can press Ctrl–K to search for trees.
I try to adhere to several principles when composing trees.

html:ul.html:li: If a definition or a lemma would present itself during a proof attempt, then do not introduce it until that part of the proof. The nature of forests makes this kind of organization more viable, as each definition is a tree by itself.
If a part of a proof has an easy constructive phrasing, use it and avoid classical reasoning. But if it requires some complication, then the classical way is used.

Avoid abstraction leaks. Even if A is defined as B, do not use them interchangeably. For instance, an ideal is defined as a subset of a ring satisfying certain conditions. But we will insist on writing ideals as numbers, for example saying \mathfrak {a} \mid x instead of x \in \mathfrak {a}. This is not too heretic, since algebraic number theory already uses this kind of notation. Similarly, although prime ideals correspond to points in \operatorname {Spec}(A), we do not identify them.
Apply unbiased terminology and negative thinking.
